title: Throttle & escrow framework for deferred batching and KV-cache recommendations
creator: Aria Chen
description:
Problem: Optimize generates batching and KV-cache suggestions that can save considerable token cost but occasionally regress tail latency or interact poorly with specific models and sequence distributions. Current auto-apply paths are either too aggressive or require manual operator intervention, creating friction for customers and missed savings.

Goal: Implement a "throttle-and-escrow" framework that sits between Optimize suggestion generation and configuration activation. The framework must provide: a deferred apply window, operator escrow (manual approval with timer), adaptive canary throttles (percent-of-traffic over time), simulated-preview (dry-run telemetry), abort thresholds tied to SLO regressions and error spikes, and automated rollback hooks. It should integrate with Console rollouts and existing rollout policies but be pluggable into both Hosted and Dedicated control planes.
acceptance_criteria: Escrow state introduced in Optimize suggestion lifecycle: suggestions can be marked 'escrowed' and will not change runtime config until released
Config can be scheduled into a deferred window (start/end) with optional operator approval timeout
Adaptive canary throttles supported: percent-of-traffic ramp plan defined per suggestion and enforced by the routing layer
Simulated-preview job produces a differential telemetry report (latency, tail-p95/p99, error-rate, cost-per-token) before live rollout
Abort policy enforces automatic rollback when latency p95 increases by more than configured percentage or error-rate exceeds threshold
Operators can force-commit or extend escrow from Console and via an API endpoint; actions are audited
End-to-end integration test covers a safe rollout scenario with synthetic traffic and a deliberate latency regression to validate rollback
Documentation + Console UI copy for the escrow flow and recommended defaults published to Confluence and Console help
tasks: Design: finalize escrow state machine and API contract (Confluence: /confluence/optimize/escrow-design)
Runtime: add flaggable 'escrowed' suggestion type and defer apply path in suggestion-applier service
Router: implement percent-ramp enforcement and throttling hooks tied to suggestion IDs
Simulator: implement simulated-preview runner that replays sample traces against proposed batching/cache config
Telemetry: wire simulated-preview and canary telemetry into Console dashboards and generate diff reports
Policy: implement abort rules engine that evaluates p95/p99/error-rate/cost deltas and triggers rollback
Console: add escrow UI, approve/extend/force-commit controls and audit timeline
E2E tests: synthetic workload that validates safe rollback and audit trail
Security: review API for approval flows and ensure RBAC checks and KMS usage for audit logs
Rollout: pilot to 5 internal customers via Dedicated pools before wider opt-in
comments: 2025-02-16 Aria Chen (creator): Initial draft of the approach. Leaning toward keeping the escrow as a first-class state so downstream services can opt-in. Linking a strawman state machine in Confluence.

2025-02-18 Mateo Rivera (assignee): Reviewed and updated tasks to include simulated-preview runner. Concern: simulator must not be expensive; propose sampling of recent traffic and low-cost model proxy for latency estimation.

2025-02-20 Priya Kapoor (PM): Good direction. Please add UX flows for operator notifications (Slack/email) when escrow timer expires. Also include default escalation (ops oncall) if manual approval not provided within business SLA.

2025-02-24 Elena Park (SRE): Observability note — we should emit a dedicated metric 'optimize.escrow.applies' and structured events for rollback reasons. Also add synthetic canary lanes to avoid cross-tenant noise.

2025-02-28 Security review (notes from Dan Li): Approvals API must require RBAC role 'optimize-admin' and write audit events to KMS-backed audit store. No config secrets stored in suggestion payloads. Add to tasks.
